svg.title: What developers should do differently
svg.desc: 1. Design the security experience: Tell customers what happened, why, and how to recover; 2. Build security circuit breakers: Suspicious bulk actions pause automatically, not just alert; 3. Design for partial unavailability: Suspend one tenant or operation, not the whole service; 4. Make operations interruptible: Long-running work can pause, cancel or reauthorize; 5. Add friction when behavior looks suspicious: Scoped keys, rate limits, less concurrency, extra auth; 6. Make restrictions survive failover: Retries, queues and backups can't route around them; 7. Measure false positives: Track interruptions, how long they last, how fast customers recover; 8. Test containment, not just detection: Simulate stolen credentials and confirm the damage stops; 9. Design for recovery: Restrictions are reversible; interrupted work resumes safely
svg.text: Tell customers what happened, why, and how to recover
Suspicious bulk actions pause automatically, not just alert
Suspend one tenant or operation, not the whole service
Long-running work can pause, cancel or reauthorize
Add friction when behavior looks suspicious
Scoped keys, rate limits, less concurrency, extra auth
Retries, queues and backups can't route around them
Track interruptions, how long they last, how fast customers recover
Simulate stolen credentials and confirm the damage stops
Restrictions are reversible; interrupted work resumes safely
